title: Add a claude -p --plugin-dir live-session probe to the release gate, asserting session.start was not skipped
description:
opum-doc seq 178 (ODOC-OP-2026-10-03-09), relayed by opum-agent, verbatim: "a `claude -p --plugin-dir` probe of each registered command against a live engine belongs in the gate." Its rule, also verbatim: "never register a slash command whose name equals a skill the same plugin ships."

WHY IT EXISTS, from this repository's own failure. The 0.13.0 board work renamed its slash command to `quest`, which is the name the plugin's own skill already owned. The engine REFUSED the registration and the whole `session.start` hook threw and was skipped, so the board never initialised -- no pane, no refresh clock. `claude plugin validate --strict` passed and the 21-test mod suite passed; nothing in the repo could see it. Only a live session showed it, as one line on stderr:

  opum-quest: session.start hook skipped: threw opum-quest: $.command.register: "/quest" refused: it is the plugin's /opum-quest:quest

Measured 2026-10-03. It is not hypothetical: the 0.13.0 tree carried it and every gate was green.

WHAT IT MUST DO, and the second clause is the one that matters, because a probe that only checks registered commands passes on exactly the tree that was broken:
1. Run `claude -p --plugin-dir <dir> "<prompt>"` against a plugin dir staged from the tree under test, from a cwd OUTSIDE that tree, for each command or tool the mod registers, and assert each one reaches the COMMAND or TOOL rather than a same-named skill.
2. Assert `session.start` printed NO "hook skipped" line. A refused registration is invisible except as that line, so its absence is the assertion.
3. Assert positively that `session.start` RAN, rather than inferring it from silence -- the shape used in the 0.13.0 verification was to ask the session to list the tools available to it and require the mod's tool to be present, since only `session.start` registers it. Silence proves nothing: a hook that never ran and a hook that ran cleanly both print nothing.
4. Assert the CLI-conflict direction too: a request naming a real CLI subcommand (for example `quest board`) must still reach the CLI, not the tool.

WHAT IS MEASURED TODAY, so the gap is not overstated: no live-session probe exists in this repository. `claude plugin validate --strict` and `claude plugin test` are what run, and `scripts/qualification/prepublish.mjs`'s `mod` gate is just `bun run test:mod`. Nothing greps stderr for a skipped hook. The probe above was run by hand during 0.13.0 and is not scripted anywhere.

WHERE IT BELONGS: release prep for a plugin release, alongside the existing qualification scripts. Fleet-wide relevance noted by opum-doc, but this task is the quest-cli half.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A script runs `claude -p --plugin-dir <staged tree> "<prompt>"` from a cwd outside the tree for every command and tool the mod registers, and reports which each request reached
It fails when session.start prints a "hook skipped" line, and fails when a registered command is refused
It asserts POSITIVELY that session.start ran, rather than treating silence as success -- a hook that never ran and a hook that ran cleanly are indistinguishable from output alone
It fails when a request naming a real CLI subcommand reaches the tool instead of the CLI
It is wired into release prep so a plugin release runs it, and it is proven both ways: red against a deliberately refused registration, green against a clean tree
